chapter: Forming the band in New York
title: Trumpets, Cat Anderson, Matthew Gee and the 22-piece band
summary: He recalls Bill Moore, Charlie Jones, Cat Anderson, Matthew Gee, Stretch Ridley and a band that grew to 22 pieces.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Bill Moore was a beautiful trumpet player. He joined me during the war days. He was a beautiful trumpet player then.
And, Charlie Jones. I got him out of Texas. He was a trumpet player there with me for awhile.

For one while, I had 5 trumpets including Cat Anderson. Cat Anderson was with the Sunset Royal band. So, man, you can imagine 5 trumpets there with Cat Anderson, and then I'm down front, it was 6. And, we were all blowing and Cat was blowing above, and I'm trying to go higher than he. You know. Now, you can imagine the styles we had there. We had those walls rocking. And so, we had a lot of fun.
Now, we get down to Matthew Gee (Unintelligible). I got him out of Detroit. I was at the

Paradise Theater. He's a beautiful trombone player. He was with me quite a few years before he went, till he went into the service. When he came out, I think he joined Duke Ellington cause I was all set.

Then, I had Bernard Flood. He replaces Jimmy Harris. Yeah. Jimmy Harris was also a trumpet player out of Birmingham. He was from Birmingham too. And Bernard Flood, I don't know where, well, he was from out of New York when I met him.

Oh, I see you have Stretch Ridley here. That was during the time when he came out of the Service. I had 5 saxes. So, when he came out of the Service, I hired him to join me then. And, at that time, I had 6 saxophones, three tenors. And I hated to see the boys come out of the Service when they with me before, until they got set, although I was set. So, I just included the whole band. At one time, I went up to about 22 pieces, and I kept that for about, oh, maybe a couple of years cause there were too many men. I had some doubling on the parts.
